summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell degranulation syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, orthostatic hypotension, anxiety, and GERD was admitted for acute-onset chest pain radiating to the back, neck, and shoulders, associated with nausea, vomiting, diaphoresis, and diarrhea. She had recently been evaluated at another hospital and returned due to worsening symptoms. Evaluation revealed no evidence of acute cardiac ischemia, pulmonary embolism, or aortic dissection on CT angiography, and serial troponins were negative. There were no objective signs of mast cell degranulation, and her symptoms improved without specific intervention. The EpiPen was temporarily withheld due to risk of hypertensive crisis given her history of epinephrine-related MI. Urinalysis showed no infection. She was discharged home asymptomatic on her prior medications with instructions to follow up with her PCP and specialists. She briefly returned to the ED post-discharge due to anxiety but was cleared and discharged again.
